Primary Question: Is this extracted article technically usable and trustworthy enough to enter the annotation pipeline?
What Must Be Built: Automated rule engine for title/body/date/canonical/source/provenance/GCS checks; extraction-quality scoring; exception queue; parser-version linkage
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Fully automated first pass using deterministic validation and anomaly rules across 100% of records
Human Review: Small human audit sample plus review of flagged anomalies/failures; humans validate the automation, not label every record
Suggested Database Objects: automated_annotations or extraction_quality_reviews linked to article_versions; auto_status, auto_reasons, rule_version, confidence, validation_status
Reviewer UI: /review/l0 focused on sampled audit and exceptions rather than routine manual labeling
Quality / Evaluation: Automated pass/review/fail rates by source; sampled human validation accuracy; parser-defect rate; false-pass/false-fail rate
Entry Criterion: Collected article version exists with provenance
Exit Criterion: Automated L0 decision stored for 100% of records; validation sample shows acceptable performance; unresolved hard failures excluded
Downstream Use: Automated corpus-quality gate before all semantic layers
Proposal / Research Link: Preprocessing, provenance verification and data-quality control

Primary Question: Is the article substantively about a Kenyan event or issue within the study population?
What Must Be Built: Gazetteer/NER evidence engine plus geographic relevance classifier; confidence thresholds; uncertainty queue
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Automated across 100% using Kenyan place/institution/demonym evidence, foreign-location evidence, NER and a classifier/score; publisher identity alone must not decide
Human Review: Small stratified validation sample across sources/languages/confidence bands; ambiguous/low-confidence cases prioritized for human review
Suggested Database Objects: automated_annotations (task_type=kenya_relevance) + human_validation; preserve suggested_label, confidence, evidence, model/rule version
Reviewer UI: /review/l1 for sample validation and uncertainty review, showing article, detected evidence and automated label
Quality / Evaluation: Accuracy/F1 against human validation sample; ambiguity rate; confidence calibration; subgroup error rate by source/language
Exit Criterion: Automated Kenya-relevance label exists for all eligible records and validation performance is acceptable
Proposal / Research Link: Target population = eligible articles reporting/discussing Kenyan events/issues

Primary Question: Does the eligible Kenyan article report or substantively discuss GBV under the approved study definition?
Label Structure: Binary model (`not_gbv=0`, `gbv=1`) + application uncertainty label `borderline`; raw confidence is p(GBV)
What Must Be Built: Weak supervision, protected human review, reviewed-only/mixed-effective dataset export, class-weighted AfroXLMR training, checksummed offline loading, required schema protections and full compatible persisted inference are implemented. Remaining work is research validation: final codebook, reproducible review sampling, independent reference membership, positive/source/language support and threshold/evaluation protocol.
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Weak coverage: 324/324 = 7/15/302; human-overlay weak view 10/312/2. Reviewed export: 300 = 3/297; mixed-effective: 322 = 10/312. `l2-afroxlmr-dev-v1` is trained. Current compatible Transformer coverage is 324/324 = 11 gbv / 307 not_gbv / 6 borderline, zero pending; development schema readiness is true.
Human Review: Weak-label review exists for the 302 originally borderline rows. Current model outputs are not an independent human reference set. Next review work should use reproducible batches, initially hide model output to reduce anchoring, preserve append-only adjudication, and keep frozen reference members/training-related duplicates separate.
Suggested Database Objects: automated_annotations + human_validations + immutable reviewed/mixed manifests are implemented; future validation batches, adjudication records and frozen reference membership must preserve exact article/version/model/codebook lineage
Reviewer UI: /annotations/l2 and /annotations/review/<annotation_id> support current weak/model inspection and protected review. Next UI/workflow additions should support reproducible batches, blinded initial decisions, adjudication and private progress/export reporting.
Quality / Evaluation: Current training loss and full-coverage counts are engineering evidence only. Final evaluation requires independent human-reference precision/recall/F1, macro-F1/AUC or PR-AUC where supported, calibration/abstention analysis and source/language subgroup evidence.
Exit Criterion: Protected independent human-reference evaluation demonstrates acceptable performance/calibration with documented error boundaries and no train/reference leakage
When to Build: Development implementation complete; structured validation/reference design is next; retraining and downstream L3/L4 follow later
Downstream Use: GBV candidate selection for later L3/L4, active learning and analytics
Proposal / Research Link: Objective 1; engineering milestone complete, research validation gate open

Primary Question: For GBV-positive articles, what form(s) of GBV are reported?
Label Structure: Multi-label probabilities + thresholded labels for approved GBV taxonomy
What Must Be Built: Automated multi-label classifier using AfroXLMR/XLM-R; taxonomy-specific output head; per-label thresholds; versioned predictions
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Automated across 100% of L2-positive records. Initial weak/rule labels can bootstrap training; final annotation is produced by the multi-label model
Human Review: Small stratified validation sample including rare classes, multi-label cases and low-confidence predictions; humans correct sampled outputs
Suggested Database Objects: model_predictions/automated_annotations with per-label probabilities, threshold version, model_version; human_validation and final_reference_labels separate
Reviewer UI: /review/l3 for validating sampled multi-label outputs, low-confidence cases and rare categories
Quality / Evaluation: Per-label precision/recall/F1, macro/micro-F1, label-support/imbalance analysis, calibration and human override rate
Entry Criterion: L2 automated GBV-positive or borderline record
Exit Criterion: Multi-label predictions stored for all included records with acceptable validation metrics and documented thresholds
When to Build: After L2 classifier baseline is available
Downstream Use: Automated GBV-type analytics and training/evaluation target
Proposal / Research Link: Proposal requires one or more applicable GBV-type categories

Primary Question: Where did the reported event occur, and which place mentions are event locations rather than contextual locations?
Label Structure: Detected spans + location role + normalized place/admin unit + confidence
What Must Be Built: Future work: versioned human span/event-role schema, gazetteer/rule place-extraction baseline, contextual NER, event-location role classifier, Kenyan gazetteer/disambiguation and geocoding
Automation / Pre-Annotation: The Kenya gazetteer and completed L2 model provide technical prerequisites, but L4 implementation is intentionally deferred until structured L2 validation/reference work begins. Existing L1 lexical geography must not be treated as NER or gold event-location labels.
Human Review: When started, sample validated GBV-positive articles across sources/languages and multi-location/ambiguous cases; review spans, event-vs-context role and normalized/geocoded admin units separately.
Suggested Database Objects: future location_predictions / extracted_locations / geocoded_locations + human_validation; preserve span offsets, role, normalized hierarchy, confidence and model/geocoder versions
Reviewer UI: /review/l4 planned; should reuse current local security/lineage principles with highlighted spans and candidate admin units
Quality / Evaluation: Entity precision/recall/F1 + exact-span match; event-role accuracy/F1; administrative-unit geocoding accuracy against independent human reference annotations
Entry Criterion: Structured L2 validation underway + usable validated GBV-positive pool
Exit Criterion: Automated location outputs produced with acceptable independent span/role/geocode validation and documented error boundaries
When to Build: After the immediate L2 validation/reference milestone; before system integration/dashboard
Downstream Use: Location evaluation and privacy-safe spatial aggregation
Proposal / Research Link: Objective 2: place extraction → event-location interpretation → geocoding

Primary Question: Does the article or derived output contain information that should be hidden, generalized or withheld?
Label Structure: Multi-label privacy-risk flags + automated action + confidence
What Must Be Built: Automated PII/risk detection using NER + regex/rules + location-precision checks; suppression/generalization policy
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Automated across 100% before downstream display/API. Use high-recall PII detection and rule-based output actions
Human Review: Small high-risk audit sample plus mandatory review of low-confidence/conflicting cases where policy requires it
Suggested Database Objects: privacy_risk_predictions / safety_flags + human_validation; action, reason, confidence, policy_version, model_version
Reviewer UI: /review/l5 for sampled high-risk validation and policy exceptions
Quality / Evaluation: Recall on known sensitive patterns, false-negative audit, override rate, audit completeness, zero unnecessary PII in public outputs
Exit Criterion: Automated safety decision attached to every displayable record; validation confirms acceptable protection
When to Build: Design alongside L2-L4; enforce before dashboard
Proposal / Research Link: Proposal requires data minimisation, privacy protection, aggregated geography and human oversight

Primary Question: How well do automated annotations match human judgement, and where does automation fail?
Label Structure: initial blinded decision + confirmed/corrected/unresolved + adjudicated/frozen reference label where available
What Must Be Built: Protected local review workspace exists. The next implementation milestone is reproducible validation batches with fixed sampling configuration/seed, initially hidden model output, separate append-only adjudication, private progress/export reporting and frozen reference membership.
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Automation should construct reproducible stratified batches across publisher, reviewed language, predicted label/confidence and difficult/borderline cases. Training articles may support error analysis but must be excluded from independent final testing along with related duplicates.
Human Review: Weak L2 has 302 recorded reviews from the development workflow; current model coverage is 324/324 but is not independently validated. Future validation must include representative confident positives/negatives as well as uncertainty cases, and must preserve a protected held-out reference cohort.
Suggested Database Objects: human_validations and development manifests now; future validation_batches, batch_membership, adjudications, reviewer metadata and frozen reference membership
Reviewer UI: Extend the current protected review UI to support batch membership, initially hidden prediction/confidence, reveal-after-initial-decision, adjudication and private progress reporting
Quality / Evaluation: Human-human agreement where double-coded support exists; model-vs-human accuracy/F1 on independent samples; override/error rates; calibration/abstention; source/language subgroup evidence; leakage checks
Entry Criterion: Automated/model predictions exist and validation codebook/sampling design is agreed
Exit Criterion: Independent validation statistics, documented error boundaries and a frozen held-out human reference set exist before thesis-level final evaluation
Downstream Use: Research validity for L0-L5 without manually labelling the full corpus

Primary Question: Can every automated label, human validation and model result be traced to its source and version?
Label Structure: dataset_version | annotation_version | model_version | validation-batch/reference membership | code_commit
What Must Be Built: Deterministic reviewed/mixed development manifests and model artifact hashes are implemented. Next: reproducible validation-batch manifests, related/near-duplicate grouping, explicit frozen reference membership, final split metadata and experiment lineage.
Automation / Pre-Annotation: All 322 mixed records were used for the first model, so they cannot serve as the independent final test set. Existing reference-exclusion support should be extended to frozen membership plus related-duplicate exclusion before evaluation.
Human Review: Researcher approves codebook and reference membership; final reference records and related duplicates remain outside training, threshold tuning, active learning and model selection.
Suggested Database Objects: private development manifests now; future validation_batch_membership, dataset_versions, split_assignment, duplicate_group_id, reference membership, model/annotation/codebook versions
Reviewer UI: Future admin/report view should show validation-batch/reference/split status and counts without exposing private article text or reviewer identity
Quality / Evaluation: No train/reference leakage; complete lineage; exact/near-duplicate control; reproducible manifests/artifacts; isolated held-out human reference set
Entry Criterion: Development model exists and structured validation design is agreed
Exit Criterion: Immutable research development/reference memberships and duplicate-aware splits exist before final comparison/evaluation
When to Build: Implement with the next structured validation milestone; continue versioning during corpus growth
Downstream Use: Reproducible experiments, error analysis and defensible final evaluation
